questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer:
I have always wanted to go to the Netherlands, especially Amsterdam. I know that Vrije Universitet is a very good University where I could expect academic challenges. I was also recommended the program by two friends, who went to Vrije last year. 
Also all of the classes were in english.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It has been all I dreamed of.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer:
I think is was quite easy - the introduction helped me. 
But I am also glad I had my friend who had gone to Vrije a year earlier to provide me with information about living in Amsterdam as a student - benefits, BSN number, housing allowance and so on. This information werent that well provided.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I didnt'

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: I think it was nice with a full week on introduction on the first week of arrival

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
Pretty easy via Vrije Universitet - DuWo. But you needed to be quick! 
First in line, first to be served concept.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Its nicer and closer to the city! Campus livings are not especially nice i think....

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
I have my own little appartment that I par quite easily because of the local housing allowance i recieve beacuse I have my own kitchen + bathroom. 
I pay half the price! 3000DKK.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Very easy - especially if you participate in the online seminars that Vrije provide prior to the registration process period.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You need to register for at least 24 ECTS in total - 12 ECTS pr period. There are 3 periods in the first semester and 3 periods in the second semester.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Mail and an international office. They were very quick in responding.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer:
100% - I got all the the courses I registered for. 
But you have to be quick. 
First in line, first to be served concept.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Be ready at 9 o'clock on the day where the registration period opens.
It is not that easy to shift once you got a spot.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
It was nice - a great work load though.... 
It could have been clearer which courses were to which field... 
Not very clear - I have ended up taking a course that is not Psychology.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer:
The course level is high and the work load as well. 
Way more than Copenhagen even though the courses are smaller (6 ECTS) and the periods a shorter (2 montsh)

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
It was nice! More smaller classes and less big lectures. 
Very interactive and easy to participate.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Period 1: 
Team processes in organizations (Pre-approved) 
Power & Organizations 

Period 2: 
Leadership in Organizations (Pre-approved)
Culture and Identity in organizations

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Team processes in organizations - very interactive, group work and an interesting topic! good teacher.  
Leadership in Organizations - very interactive, group work and an interesting topic! good teacher.  
Culture and Identity in organizations - very interactive, group work and an interesting topic! good teacher.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: There were some taxes that you need to pay living in Amsterdam - but you can apply for economic help through the municipalty - quite a process though....

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
Housing - if you reciewe housing allowance. 
Food is also a little cheaper

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There are a lot of opputinites at Vrije! Both social and academic and Vrije is VERY international

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: All of the above mentioned!

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I actually did'nt attend any....

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go to museums, flea markets, food markets and visit near by citites such as Utrecht, Harleem, Haag and so on.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy - it is quite similar to danish culture but more multicultural

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I found most of my friends in my housing and that has been nice that they live right next to me.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer:
The dutch people are even more direct than danes haha. The service at restaurants are quite dissapointing. 
The bike even crazier than danes and NO ONE wears bike helmets. Be aware.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The multicultral vibe

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Be prerared for quite a work load 
Apply for housing allowance (if you have you own apartment) as soon as possible after recieving the BSN number. 
Participate in the intro week.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer:
It is hard to get prea-approval of the courses, so start the process early on! 
Dont have to many visits from home, haha.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: All the english I have spoken and trying living by myself in a new country!

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: I misses my friends, family and boyfriend.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
